questions.question: Describe the difference between intrusive and extrusive igneous rocks.
questions.solution_html:
• Intrusive (Plutonic) Rocks: 4 marks
  • o Form beneath the Earth’s surface.
  • o Slow cooling → large, coarse-grained crystals (e.g., granite).
  • o High visibility mineral grains.
  • Extrusive (Volcanic) Rocks: 4 marks
  • o Form on or above the surface.
  • o Rapid cooling → fine-grained or glassy texture (e.g., basalt).
  • o May contain vesicles due to trapped gas.

questions.question: Describe metamorphism, and how does it differ from igneous and sedimentary processes.
questions.solution_html:
• Metamorphism
  • Process that alters the mineral composition and texture of rocks due to heat, pressure, and
  • chemically active fluids, without melting. 3 marks
  • Differences
  • Metamorphic vs Igneous
  • o Igneous rocks form from complete melting and solidification, while metamorphism
  • occurs in the solid state. 3 marks
  • Metamorphic vs Sedimentary
  • o Sedimentary processes involve weathering, erosion, deposition, and lithification
  • while metamorphism alters pre-existing rocks through heat and pressure. 3 marks
  • Textures
  • o Metamorphic rocks show foliated structures (e.g., schist, gneiss) unlike sedimentary
  • bedding or igneous crystalline textures. 3 marks
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: bedding or igneous crystalline textures.
